plain.text: A prayer for the king before battle: "May the LORD answer you when you are in distress; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you." May he send help from his sanctuary, remember your offerings, give you the desire of your heart and make your plans succeed. "May we shout for joy over your victory."

"Now this I know: the LORD gives victory to his anointed." "Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God." They will fall, but we rise up and stand firm. "LORD, give victory to the king! Answer us when we call!"

summary.bigIdea: God's people pray for their king and remember that real security comes from trusting God, not in military power.
points: The people pray for God to answer and help their king in trouble.
"Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God."
They are confident that God hears and helps.
summary.reflection: What are the "chariots and horses" people trust in today? What do you find yourself relying on?
